column2: This campaign has been designed to reflect fast pace, heavy and continuous action. The armies are also significantly stronger than in reality. We all know the AI plays awful, so I have to change the scenarios in a way it can at least play a decent game. All the scenarios co n tain many over strengthened units, entrenchment, leaders, etc. In several scenarios the player will be allowed to deploy only a fraction of its army. The auxiliary units are very important because they contribute to the balance of power and at the same t ime provide some sorely needed capabilities. At the same time the game becomes more realistic. Successful campaign play requires minimum casualties or you will be out pretty soon. This fact leads to neglect of the auxiliary units and excessive caution concerning the core units. Here you cannot neglect your auxiliary units. You will need every single one of them or you will not win. I regularly reinforced them to keep them alive.

column2: I did all the work, so, I have taken the prerogative of designing the kind of scenarios I like, full of action , and fast pace even if that strains reality. I hated the Winter Storm scenario in the original SSI campaign when it takes forever for those Romanian units to reach the last victory hex. I also do not like scenarios where after 3-4 turns you can put aut omatic pilot and collect a victory without any thinking. There are surprises lurking for you at every corner.

column2: One interesting concept used in this campaign is the idea of "defensive scenarios." There are several of these scenarios in the campaign. The main idea is that in order to win the player has to keep all the victory objectives held by him at the beginning of the game. If some are lost the player has to retake them to win. Some extra victory scenarios have been added to avoid a technical proble m . If you do not have victory scenarios of your own a victory can be achieved by taken any hex owned by your opponent. Of course, this fact can lead to premature victories. The premature victory can be avoided by adding at least a victory scenario for t he player. Normally I have added the supply hexes for the AI player.

column2: I have organized implicitly the two armies following these guidelines. The two armies are distributed in Corps, infantry and tank corps. A tank corps has 4-6 units, 3-4 are tanks the others are auxiliaries (anti-tanks, AD, etc.). Each infantry corps has 4-8 units. At least 3 are infantry units, the others are artillery, anti-tanks, AA, AD, etc. Every unit represents a division or division-like formation. You start with a reinforced mixed Corps. Later on you will, explicitly or implicitly, build one Tank Corp and up to two Infantry Corps.
